text.p: Bonds were recovering as Europe in general advanced apparently feeling the worries over the launch of the single currency were receding slightly, traders said.
Futures were leading the advance, largely on technical reasons due to the approaching expiry of the June contract.
The futures were seen as being relatively cheaper than the cash equivalent, so traders were opting for the derivative rather than buy the cash against delivery at the June 16 expiry, they said.
"The speculators who were previously very pessimistic about the question of the single currency are short and as the expiry is approaching, they are in the market buying," said one trader.
"This trend is going to continue, particularly if the cash rises more today," said another trader.
Traders said they saw the spread with the 10-year cash Bund remaining around 68 basis points.
